variant_equivalence.method: Reused the existing whole-image byte-diff audits (autopilot-868-vs-915-diff.json, mando-868-vs-915-diff.json) rather than re-running per-variant census -- any dispatch/builder logic difference would show up as a code difference in those diffs, and none did beyond the two already-documented non-protocol items.
variant_equivalence.autopilot_868_vs_915: IDENTICAL protocol family set. The two 70,768-byte images differ in exactly one 4-byte RF center-frequency .data constant; every dispatcher/builder instruction (ASCII chain, 0xF0/0xE0 gate, event dispatcher) is byte-identical.
variant_equivalence.mando_868_vs_915: IDENTICAL protocol family set. The large raw-byte diff resolves entirely to one link-time function-relocation artifact (every internal reference shifted by a constant +0x10-class offset, external call targets unchanged) plus two cosmetic strings (RF-band label, build timestamp) -- confirmed directly for FUN_00010ce4/FUN_00010cf4 (the Remote's inbound dispatcher itself) in mando-868-vs-915-diff.json.
variant_equivalence.genuine_protocol_differences_found: NONE. R17 (radio transport boundary) is the only 'DIFFERENT' row in the four-firmware reconciliation matrix, and it is explicitly the RF band constant, not a protocol family difference -- excluded here per this task's own instruction not to treat relocation/layout differences as protocol differences.

autopilot_rx_accepts_J.evidence: ascii_dispatcher (0x8258 chain), character check at 0x88b2 (cmp r3,#0x4a / 'J'), branch to 0x88b6-... calling FUN_00007868 or FUN_000077f8 (motor-driver disable sequences) under two sub-condition flags -- see docs/replacement/mapped-pin-causal-gap-audit.json's PB06/PB07 candidate for the full disable-path trace (not re-derived here, cited only).

remote_tx_emits_J.evidence: CONCRETELY RE-VERIFIED this session: mando868 FUN_00005a50 sends the literal bytes 'J|\0' (dumped directly from flash: 4a 7c 00) three times via the shared TX wrapper FUN_000058a8. FUN_00005a50 has 12 callers across the image (FUN_0000b680/G-builder, FUN_0000ba98/&-query, FUN_0000c340, FUN_0000c440/S-!-handler, FUN_0000cfc8/RUNNING-renderer, FUN_0000d988, FUN_0000db34 x4, FUN_0000fa10/T-status-redraw, FUN_0000fdf0/boot) -- this is NOT a single dedicated UI action's sender; it is a GENERIC post-request postamble called after many different transactions complete, mirroring H's role as the generic preamble (FUN_00005a14, per command-inventory.md). This matches and concretely strengthens the existing static-inventory row (commands.csv id=J, remote_site=0x5a50, confidence=medium-high) rather than contradicting it.

remote_rx_understands_a_J_response.evidence: No AutoPilot-side pending-event write (no 'pending[N]=1'-shaped instruction) was visible in the 0x88b2 J-handling disassembly examined in the prior causal-gap-audit session, unlike G/S/!/& which each explicitly arm a pending-event slot consumed by the 0x9268 outbound dispatcher. No Remote-side 'J-response' parser or literal was found in any existing evidence.

surprises_and_gaps: H and J are not independent user-facing commands: both are generic transaction pre/postambles (FUN_00005a14 / FUN_00005a50) called around many unrelated request-response transactions (G, &, S/!, T-status redraw, boot), not a single dedicated UI action each.

'MS' exists as TWO completely unrelated families on opposite directions: EVENT16_MS (AutoPilot->Remote, literal 'MS' no pipe, connection/state transition) and MS_REMOTE (Remote->AutoPilot, 'MS|' with pipe, no AutoPilot RX match). Same two letters, unrelated code paths -- flagged explicitly to prevent future conflation.

B_UNKNOWN: the Remote's inbound dispatcher has a real, non-trivial parser case for a leading 'B' byte with no known AutoPilot producer anywhere in the 18-event dispatcher, MT, or T -- a genuine orphan on the Remote-RX side, already noted in two existing docs but not previously surfaced as a protocol-census family in its own right.

D's AutoPilot-side round trip (RX, persist to flash, reload on fresh boot) is execution-confirmed, but its Remote-side producer was never located -- a case where 'transaction concretely proven' and 'producer confirmed' are genuinely different claims that must not be conflated.

The event7 (BANG response) 11-vs-10 field mismatch is a real, silent, confirmed-on-both-sides protocol discrepancy, not a documentation gap -- already known, restated here because it is exactly the class of 'variant-mismatch' this census exists to catch.

J's Remote-side sender (FUN_00005a50) was concretely re-verified this session (byte-for-byte flash dump of the 'J|' literal plus its 3x send and 12 call sites) -- strengthens, does not contradict, the existing medium-high-confidence static-inventory row.
